notes: Washington's work rules for 16- and 17-year-olds, for anyone who says they're in high school or under 18. Shown as a support service beside routes.
All wording comes from L&I's current pages. Washington's child labor rules changed on July 1, 2026, so older L&I news articles were not used.

The variance sentence uses L&I's exact framing: registered apprentices and student-learners in an approved CTE worksite learning program 'may be granted limited exemptions from some' prohibitions. It does not say a program lifts restrictions.
L&I's student-learner variance page confirms 16- and 17-year-olds can take part in Washington registered apprenticeship programs.
Every quote is re-checked against its live page on each sync. Set status to 'reviewed' and fill reviewed_by / reviewed_on to load this record.

programs.name: Washington work rules for 16- and 17-year-olds (L&I)
programs.organization: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries
programs.summary: Before a 16- or 17-year-old starts work, the employer needs a minor work permit endorsement and a parent/school authorization form signed by the employer, the teen, a school official, and a parent or guardian; the form expires every September 30 and must be renewed. During a school week, 16- and 17-year-olds may work up to 4 hours a day and 20 hours a week, between 7 a.m. and 10 p.m., or up to 28 hours with a special variance signed by a parent and school representative. Some duties are prohibited for minors; registered apprentices and student-learners in an approved CTE worksite learning program may be granted limited exemptions from some of those prohibitions. 16- and 17-year-olds can take part in Washington registered apprenticeship programs.

source.name: L&I: How to Hire Minors
source.authority: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries

quotes: Employers must have a current minor work permit endorsement for each location where minors are employed.
Parent/school authorization forms must be signed by the employer, the minor, an official from the minor's school, and the minor's parent or legal guardian.
All parent/school authorization forms expire each new school year on the 30th day of September and must be renewed annually.

quotes.text: School week 4 hours * 20 hours 6 days 7 a.m. - 10 p.m.
School week with special variance 6 hours * 28 hours
Employers only need to have the minor’s parent or legal guardian and school representative sign the special variance section
Registered apprenticeships and student-learners in an approved Career Technical Education (CTE) Worksite Learning program may be granted limited exemptions from some of these prohibitions.
A student-learner variance allows 16- and 17-year-olds participating in a Washington State Registered Apprenticeship program
